title: Saddle Point Properties of a Hyperbolic Paraboloid
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For the hyperbolic paraboloid z = y^2 - x^2, verify that the origin (0, 0, 0) is a critical saddle point by examining partial derivatives.
finalAnswer: \nabla z(0, 0) = \mathbf{0}; \quad \text{Parabolas open upward in } y \text{ and downward in } x

steps.title: Compute First Partial Derivatives
steps.explanation: Differentiate z with respect to x and y independently.

steps.title: Evaluate at the Origin
steps.explanation: Both partial derivatives vanish at (0, 0), confirming a critical point.

steps.title: Analyze Curvatures Along Coordinate Axes
steps.mathExpression: x = 0 \implies z = y^2 \; (\text{min at } 0); \quad y = 0 \implies z = -x^2 \; (\text{max at } 0)
steps.explanation: The surface curves upward along the y-axis and downward along the x-axis, creating a classic saddle.
